definitions.formation_proof_object: A sealed, independently verifiable artifact establishing that declared conditions must hold across every execution path derivable from a specific source artifact, formed before any execution exists. It establishes that conditions must hold; it does not record that conditions held during any specific execution.
definitions.externally_verifiable_artifact: An artifact structured so that an independent party -- with access only to the artifact itself and publicly declared anchors -- can verify its integrity and interpret its declared content without requiring access to the originating system, its operators, its runtime context, or the producer's explanation. Verification conditions are declared in public_anchors.

controlling_test: Interoperability must increase reviewability without silently transferring authority across layers.

timing_axis.description: Operates before any execution bind exists. The temporal anchor is the source artifact, not a bind event: the proof is formed when the system is formed and holds for every execution path derivable from that source. It exists prior to and independent of any specific execution instantiation. Does not operate at bind or post-bind, and does not attach to any individual execution.

does: Seals formation-time proofs over a source artifact into a signed manifest: a cost ceiling, ordering laws, and cardinality bounds, each established by an SMT solver before any execution exists

Carries a self-contained offline verifier so a third party verifies the seal and the bound claims with a cryptography library and a standard runtime only, with no solver and no vendor software in the verification path
Where a coverage claim is bound, carries an algebraic certificate the verifier re-derives and checks by rational arithmetic, solver-free on the consumer side

Binds each new proof to its predecessor by signed digest and walks the chain to genesis under fail-closed conditions, discharging coverage, region containment, and net containment through one re-derivable certificate mechanism
Emits per-run conformance certificates that check an execution trace against the formation envelope as separate artifacts, bound to the formation proof by digest reference and never folded into it
does_not: Resolve admissibility at bind -- that is the boundary layer function
Preserve evidence of governed-state conditions surrounding a boundary crossing -- that is the witness layer function
Record behavioral history -- that is the substrate layer function
Stabilize responsibility-bearing closure states -- that is the closure layer function
Test artifacts of other layers for independent reviewability -- that is the reviewability layer function
Enforce, authorize, halt, or intervene in execution
Attest the behavior of any specific execution
Certify that the system is safe or compliant with any regulation
Validate the adequacy of the declared conditions themselves -- the proof establishes consequence from declarations, not the merit of the declarations

claims_boundary.authoritative_layer_claim: Formation establishes, before any execution exists, that declared conditions must hold across every execution path derivable from a specific source artifact, sealed as an independently verifiable proof object.
explicit_non_claims: Does not attest any specific execution
Does not certify overall system safety
Does not validate the adequacy of declared conditions
Does not hold or transfer execution authority
claims_boundary.consumer_boundary_constraint: Consumers must not interpret formation outputs as execution authorization, runtime approval, execution-conformance attestation, certification of regulatory compliance, or certification of system safety. A proof that declared conditions must hold across all execution paths must not be re-interpreted as evidence that any particular execution occurred or conformed.

interoperability_doctrine: GLM does not create interoperability through integration agreements. GLM creates interoperability through independently readable boundary declarations.

composition.composition_note: Formation composes with each functional type by function, per the accepted rationale Section 8. A boundary layer is the principal downstream consumer: a formation proof is one admissibility condition resolved at bind, never the admissibility resolution itself. Composability declarations are unilateral; this manifest declares the EVIDE closure manifest, which declares formation reciprocally.

public_anchors.label: GLM specification (formation accepted, schema 1.1, carries rationale digest)

machine_readable_status.boundary_readiness_note: Values: stable | provisional | experimental. Stable indicates the layer definition and schema are versioned, publicly documented, and not subject to undeclared breaking changes.
machine_readable_status.reviewability_state_note: Values: portable | partial | environment_dependent. Portable indicates artifacts are independently verifiable without access to the originating system.
machine_readable_status.authority_dependency_note: Authority over the adequacy of the declared conditions rests with the source author, not with the formation layer. The proof establishes consequence from the declarations; it does not validate their merit, and it holds no execution authority.

manifest_integrity.historically_anchored_note: Anchoring refers to the practice of archiving each published version with its computed digest at the time of publication, enabling independent reconstruction of the version history. The specific anchoring mechanism is left to the implementor in v1.0 and may be specified in future schema revisions.
manifest_integrity.note: This manifest is versioned, hashable, and historically anchored. It may be updated and superseded. Each published version should be independently archived with its digest at publication time.

glm_compatibility.non_breaking_addition_policy: minor version increment, backward compatible within major version
glm_compatibility.note: This manifest declares layer_type formation, introduced in schema 1.1. A reader limited to schema 1.0 cannot interpret the formation type; minimum_supported is therefore 1.1, not 1.0.

manifest_digest.canonicalization_method: SHA-256 over the manifest text as served with manifest_digest.value set to the placeholder string <computed-at-publish-time> and, when a signature is present, manifest_signature.value set to the placeholder string <signed-at-publish-time>, during computation. A verifier reverses both substitutions on the served bytes and recomputes.
manifest_digest.note: SHA-256 digest of the canonical JSON at publication time. Verifies content integrity. Distinct from a cryptographic signature.

manifest_signature.note: Ed25519 signature over the 32-byte manifest digest, binding the digest to the signer identity in public_key (raw key, base64). Independently checkable with a cryptography library and a standard runtime only. The digest verifies content integrity; this signature verifies authorship. It does not prove any claim in this manifest.
